learnings: Persistence is real but mostly in the cash prices, not in futures: monthly announced price changes have autocorrelation Class III milk 0.13, Class IV milk 0.41, Cheese 0.13, Butter 0.29, Nonfat dry milk 0.48, Dry whey 0.69 (an average of a random walk alone gives about 0.25); weekly futures returns have Class III milk 0.06, Class IV milk 0.12, Cheese 0.08, Butter 0.07, Nonfat dry milk 0.17, Dry whey -0.07. Futures already price most of the cash persistence.

Class III milk: best forecast of the futures error is 'Fitted share of (cash + seasonal) gap' (out-of-sample R² -3.8% vs the futures price, right on direction 40.4% of the time, month-clustered t -3.09).

Class IV milk: best forecast of the futures error is 'Fitted share of (cash + seasonal) gap' (out-of-sample R² -5.6% vs the futures price, right on direction 51.3% of the time, month-clustered t 0.84).
Cheese: best forecast of the futures error is 'Fitted share of (cash + seasonal) gap' (out-of-sample R² -1.3% vs the futures price, right on direction 47.6% of the time, month-clustered t -0.75).
Butter: best forecast of the futures error is 'Ridge: stocks, production, exports, use' (out-of-sample R² +1.7% vs the futures price, right on direction 58.2% of the time, month-clustered t 1.01).

Nonfat dry milk: best forecast of the futures error is 'Fitted share of the spot nowcast gap' (out-of-sample R² -8.1% vs the futures price, right on direction 47.9% of the time, month-clustered t -2.92).
Dry whey: best forecast of the futures error is 'Ridge: stocks, production, exports, use' (out-of-sample R² +1.7% vs the futures price, right on direction 55.0% of the time, month-clustered t 2.21).

Supply and demand (ERS stocks vs normal, production, exports, domestic use) forecast the next 3 months of announced prices with out-of-sample R² Class III milk -21%, Class IV milk -13%, Cheese -14%, Butter -9%, Nonfat dry milk -17%, Dry whey -28%; momentum alone: Class III milk -12%, Class IV milk -3%, Cheese -8%, Butter -8%, Nonfat dry milk -7%, Dry whey +10%.
